To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Hsp90 promotes the stability of LMK1 by promoting its homodimerization, which is required for its kinase activity.
Hsp90 is required for LIMK1 dimerization and stability.
LIMK1 half‐life is regulated by Hsp90 and that Hsp90 promotes LIMK1 homo‐dimer formation and phosphorylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of Hsp90 function and its role in the regulation of the LIMK family of serine/threonin protein kinases.
the regulation of actin polymerization by LIMK1 and the role of LIMK in cancer progression and metastasis.
the regulation of actin dynamics by Rho GTPases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hsp90 inhibitor 17AAG, in a dose‐dependent manner, inhibits LIMK1 phosphorylation and LIMK1‐mediated cofilin phosphorylation.
LIMK is a HSP90‐dependent protein.
Hsp90 increases the LIMK activity by promoting the LIMK homodimer formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LIMK1 stability is dependent on Hsp90.
we have identified a novel function of Hsp90 in promoting the homodimerization of LIMK.
we have demonstrated that Hsp90 regulates LIM kinase  1 (LIM kinase 1) stability and activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the half‐lives of many kinases are regulated by Hsp90, and that Hsp90 is required for homodimerization of many kinase pairs, such as ErbB‐3/ErbB‐4, ErbB‐4/HER‐2, and LIM kinase 4/LIM kinase 1.
Hsp90 stabilizes the LIMK protein by promoting its dimerization.
Hsp90 stabilizes the LIMK protein by promoting the formation of its homo‐dimers.
